claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr forms a BCC solid solution.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of approximately 855 MPa.
The proposed intervention replaces 50% of the Mo content with V to make approximately Hf(Mo0.5V0.5)TaTiZr.
The modified Hf-Mo-V-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will retain a similar single-phase BCC solid solution.
The modified alloy will have lattice parameters comparable to those of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will retain short-range order comparable to that of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Vanadium has a lower atomic mass than molybdenum.
Replacing part of the Mo with V will reduce the alloy's overall density.
Vanadium has atomic-size and electronic characteristics sufficiently similar to Mo to preserve the relevant strengthening effects.
Solid-solution, lattice-distortion, and precipitation strengthening are responsible for the high room- and elevated-temperature yield strength of the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have a density 5–10% below the baseline, approximately 9.2–9.7 g/cm³.
At 25 °C and approximately 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹ in compression, the modified alloy's yield strength will remain within 10% of 1600 MPa.
At approximately 1000 °C and 1×10⁻³ s⁻¹ in compression, the modified alloy's yield strength will remain within 10% of 855 MPa.
A V-containing refractory alloy can exhibit a single BCC phase and substantial compressive yield strength from room temperature through 900 °C.
The experiment will compare the modified alloy with a baseline made by the same casting and processing route, using density, phase, microstructure, and compression measurements.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases by less than 5% or if yield strength at either 25 °C or approximately 1000 °C falls by more than 10% from the stated baseline.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator specifies a single-phase BCC solid solution, while the mechanism invokes retention of precipitation strengthening without identifying any precipitate phase; precipitation strengthening is not internally established for the proposed single-phase state.
